I wanted to give this plain front yard a premium upgrade, so I grabbed my tools and got to work! Watching the real progress unfold in this timelapse is incredibly satisfying. Here is a step-by-step breakdown of how I built this modern rock garden: 1️⃣ First, I mapped out a smooth, curved border on the grass using white spray paint. 2️⃣ Next, I dug out the edge along the line and laid down a heavy-duty black weed barrier. 3️⃣ I installed a sleek stone border, block by block, to keep everything neat and contained. 4️⃣ Then came the best part—pouring and leveling tons of crisp white river rocks for that beautiful, high-contrast look. 5️⃣ Finally, I styled the space by placing a dark statement sphere, planting some architectural agaves, and adding solar pathway lights. Seeing the before and after of this build progress makes all the hard work totally worth it! I was called in to replace the fence panels and totally rip out the garden  (not the posts, they are a bit crooked but they are still standing😅)  I started with the fence panels, then began to totally clear the area of weeds and any other debris in the garden.  We added 2 railway sleepers at the back for a little flower bed. Then a thick layer of top soil was spread and we rolled out the turf. Then we moved 4 tonnes of hardcore to the back through the house!  Backbreaking stuff.  Thanks to my pal @Wagwarn Abel for jumping on and giving me a hand 🙏 This is obviously unfinished but I think the owner was going to slab the rest himself, so our job is done here for now! As always I wanna know what would YOU do now? There's a bed at the back that's totally empty! Most gardens don’t feel off because the plants are ugly. They feel off because the plants belong to different landscape typologies. Every plant comes from a larger visual world. Woodland plants create layered, shaded spaces. Meadow plants are airy and dynamic. Mediterranean plants are sculptural and drought-adapted. Prairie plants are upright and wind-swept. Each evokes a different feeling. When you mix plants from completely different design languages, the garden starts telling conflicting stories. A hosta beside blue fescue or lavender next to canna can feel disjointed, even if each plant is beautiful on its own. The best gardens aren’t always made of plants from the same region. They’re made of plants that create the same atmosphere. Instead of asking, “Do these colors go together?” ask, “Do these plants belong to the same world?” Great gardens aren’t collections of beautiful plants. They’re cohesive places built around a shared design language. #landscapedesign #gardendesign #gardenideas #gardeninspiration
